content.title: Port your number
content.subtitle: Bring the number your customers already know -- texting and calling.
content.intro: Porting takes about 2-4 weeks, and your current provider controls most of that timeline. Keep your number active with them until the port is finished -- cancelling early is the most common cause of delays.

sections.heading: Porting or hosting
sections.body: Two ways to bring a number into Salesmsg. Keeping your phone system and adding texting? Choose hosting. Want Salesmsg handling calls too? Choose porting. Not sure? Ask your Onboarding Manager.

rows.label: Porting
rows.value: Texting and calling move to Salesmsg. You leave your provider. Takes 2-4 weeks.

rows.label: Hosting
rows.value: Only texting comes to Salesmsg. Calling stays where it is. Takes 2-3 business days.

sections.heading: What to gather first
sections.body: Having everything ready before you submit keeps the port moving. Anything missing or mismatched sends the request back to the start.

rows.label: Phone number(s)
rows.value: Every number you want to move -- local, toll-free, VoIP and landline.

rows.label: Account info
rows.value: Account number and PIN from your current provider. No PIN? Last four of the SSN.

rows.label: Name & address
rows.value: Company name or first/last name, plus the full service address.

rows.label: Signed LOA
rows.value: Letter of Authorization, signed and returned as a PDF.

rows.label: Proof of ownership
rows.value: A bill from the last 30 days showing the number, or a provider screenshot.

sections.heading: Match your provider's records
sections.body: The name, address and account number on your request are checked against what your current provider has on file. A shortened business name or an old address is enough to get the port rejected. Check every detail before you submit.

sections.heading: How to port your number
sections.body: Five steps from start to finish.

rows.label: 1. Gather documents
rows.value: Collect account details, signed LOA and proof of ownership.

rows.label: 2. Confirm compliance
rows.value: Local U.S. numbers need A2P 10DLC approval in your Salesmsg account.

rows.label: 3. Keep number active
rows.value: Don't cancel your current service -- a disconnected number can't be ported.

rows.label: 4. Submit request
rows.value: Send via the porting form, live chat or support@salesmessage.com.

rows.label: 5. Reply quickly
rows.value: If carriers request a correction, a same-day reply can save a week.

rows.label: Verizon
rows.value: One number per port request. We'll process multiples separately.

rows.label: Google Voice
rows.value: Unlock in settings first. Keep active throughout the port.

rows.label: Twilio
rows.value: Separate, faster path -- about 3-5 business days.

rows.label: Personal mobile
rows.value: Not recommended -- your phone loses its number during setup.

rows.label: Message history
rows.value: Doesn't come with it. Export from your old provider first.

rows.label: Local U.S. sync
rows.value: May need up to 3 business days for 10DLC sync. Error 30034 resolves itself.

rows.label: Toll-free numbers
rows.value: Must be verified in Salesmsg before sending texts.

rows.label: 10DLC approval
rows.value: Doesn't transfer. Once your Salesmsg account is approved, new numbers are covered.

sections.heading: Quick answers
bullets: No fee to port. Additional lines are $5 per month each.
Your number stays active with your current provider until the port completes.
To port out later, your new provider starts the request. Ask us for your CSR.

cta.text: Reach out to our team at support@salesmessage.com or live chat.
